newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian she-devils mock Miss World.
newsitem.headline: Indian she-devils mock Miss World.

text.p: Protests against Miss World took a theatrical turn on Monday, as nine Indian actresses dressed as she-devils from Hindu mythology cavorted down the streets of Bangalore mocking the beauty pageant.
The protest would have come as some relief to organisers of the show which is being held in the southern Indian city.

Other protests have included threats by some traditionalist women's groups to commit suicide by burning themselves and threats to torch the cricket stadium where Miss World will be crowned on November 23.
One man set himself ablaze in Madurai, in the adjoining state of Tamil Nadu last week, to protest against the pageant.
"We are not against protests but they should be peaceful," said Sanjeev Gupta, chief executive of Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd, the Indian company which holds the licence to stage this year's event.
Organisers are awaiting a court decision on a petition by a women's group to ban the show. Other efforts to stop Miss World through the courts have failed.
"I am reasonably confident the show will go on. We are awaiting the court verdict," Gupta said.
There have also been protests from parties of varying political hues.
Protesters have denounced the show as an affront to women and as a cultural invasion of foreign values.
The nine women were part of a march organised by a state parliament legislator whose party platform is to promote the regional Kannada culture and language.

"This is commercialisation of beauty. It is exploitation of beauty. The judges who will choose Miss World know little of Indian culture where women are treated on a par with mothers," the legislator Vatal Nagaraj said.
Nagaraj said he plans another protest the day of the final.
A nude cut-out of Indian film star Amitabh Bachchan, the man responsible for bringing Miss World to India, would be the centrepiece of the procession, he said.
